questions.question: Crossover mirrors help a school bus driver see:

options.text: The danger zones in front of the bus.
The rear bumper.
The left side of the bus.
Vehicles in front of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The danger zones in front of the bus.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors help the driver see the danger zones in front of the bus and on the left and right sides. These areas extend from the front of the bus to the service door.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle, you must show each of the following, except:

options.text: That the oil pressure gauge is working.
That the oil pressure warning light turns off, or the gauge shows normal oil pressure.
That the oil temperature gauge, if equipped, reaches normal operating temperature.
That the oil pressure gauge turns on when brakes are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the oil pressure gauge turns on when brakes are used.
questions.explanation: When checking the oil pressure gauge, you must ensure it works. The gauge should show normal oil pressure, or the warning light should turn off. If the bus has an oil temperature gauge, it should gradually warm to the normal operating range.

questions.question: Properly adjusted mirrors on a school bus allow the driver to see ____ behind the bus.

options.text: One bus length
Two bus lengths
Three bus lengths
Four bus lengths

questions.correctAnswerText: Four bus lengths
questions.explanation: Proper mirror adjustment is very important for safe bus operation. The flat mirrors should be adjusted so the driver can see 200 feet, or four bus lengths, behind the bus.

questions.question: If driving a school bus, your four-way flashers should:

options.text: Turn on before crossing railroad tracks.
Never be used.
Only turn on after crossing railroad tracks.
Only turn on near railroad tracks if a train is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on before crossing railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: When driving a school bus, turn on your four-way flashers when you approach and cross railroad tracks. Turn them off after your entire bus has cleared the tracks.

questions.question: If a school bus needs to be evacuated, passengers should:

options.text: Always use the rear door.
Always use the windows.
Always use the front door.
Use the safest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the safest exit.
questions.explanation: If the bus needs to be evacuated in an emergency, the driver must quickly decide which exit or exits are safest and direct students to use those exits.

questions.question: When students are boarding a school bus, the driver should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Tell students when it is safe to board.
Count the students at the bus stop and make sure all have boarded.
Allow students to board in pairs.
Check all mirrors for students running toward the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow students to board in pairs.
questions.explanation: Students must always board in a single line.

questions.question: If a bus has outside convex mirrors, they will be located:

options.text: Below the outside flat mirrors.
Above the outside flat mirrors.
Next to the door.
On top of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Below the outside flat mirrors.
questions.explanation: Outside convex mirrors are located below the flat mirrors. They help the driver see a wide view of traffic, clearance, and students around the bus.

questions.question: When taking the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Wear your safety belt.
Obey all traffic signs.
Complete the test without an accident.
Use your cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, you must drive safely and responsibly. Wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs and laws, and complete the test without any accidents or violations.

questions.question: If exiting a bus during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must:

options.text: Keep both hands on the handrail.
Not touch the handrail.
Hold the handrail firmly.
Rush down the stairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handrail firmly.
questions.explanation: When exiting the bus during the basic vehicle control skills test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. If testing in a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: After students unload at a school, the driver:

options.text: May assume students have taken all their belongings.
Should assume students have left the doorway.
Should walk through the bus to check for any sleeping or hiding students.
May turn off the dispatch radio.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should walk through the bus to check for any sleeping or hiding students.
questions.explanation: After students exit the bus at school, the driver should walk through the bus to check for any students who may be sleeping or hiding. Also look for any items students may have left behind.

questions.question: The front of an enclosed trailer should:

options.text: Be swept clean.
Contain rags.
Not be used for cargo.
Be free of cracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be free of cracks.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, check the front of the trailer for damage. Look for cracks, bulges, or holes.

questions.question: During the straight line backing exercise, how many times can you exit the vehicle to check its position?

options.text: One time
Two times
Three times
Four times

questions.correctAnswerText: One time
questions.explanation: During the straight line backing exercise, you can exit your vehicle to check its position only one time.

questions.question: If you must back up at a student pick-up point, you should:

options.text: Back up before the students board the bus.
Let the students board the bus first, then back up.
Let half the students board, then back up toward the other half.
Tell the students to wait, then back toward the stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the students board the bus first, then back up.
questions.explanation: If you must back up a school bus at a pick-up point, pick up all students first. Then back up. Watch carefully for students who arrive late.

questions.question: When should a bus start moving after students have boarded?

options.text: As soon as the students are through the door
When the students are near their seats but still standing
When the students are seated and looking forward
As soon as the students cross the standee line

questions.correctAnswerText: When the students are seated and looking forward
questions.explanation: Wait until all students are seated and looking forward before you move the bus.

questions.question: After driving under an overpass during the driving skills test, you may be asked to recall:

options.text: The posted clearance.
The posted weight limit.
The width of the opening.
If there was a shoulder near the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The posted clearance.
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, your examiner may ask you to recall the posted clearance or height of an overpass you drove under.

questions.question: An outside convex mirror is properly adjusted if:

options.text: You can see at least one lane of traffic and the entire side of the bus.
You can see the front bumper.
You can see the top of the bus.
You can see the front windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see at least one lane of traffic and the entire side of the bus.
questions.explanation: The outside convex mirrors should let you see the front of the rear tires on the ground, both sides of the bus up to the mirror, and at least one traffic lane on each side.

questions.question: Before leaving a bus stop, a driver should:

options.text: Make sure no students are running to catch the bus.
Make sure students have placed their backpacks in the aisle.
Make sure students have opened the emergency vent.
Make sure students are facing the rear of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure no students are running to catch the bus.
questions.explanation: Before pulling away from a bus stop, check that no students are running toward the bus.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections should be done:

options.text: Differently each time, emphasizing different items.
The same way each time so you don't forget anything.
Once in a while.
By someone other than the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you don't forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This helps you remember all the important steps.

questions.question: A school bus stop:

options.text: Can be added by the driver if students get notice of the change.
Should be voted on by students and parents.
Should change frequently.
Should be established by the school and not changed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be established by the school and not changed.
questions.explanation: Never change or add a stop without written approval from school district officials.

questions.question: Which of the following is not acceptable emergency equipment?

options.text: Three red reflective triangles
Six fuses
Three liquid burning flares
Four yellow squares

questions.correctAnswerText: Four yellow squares
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, acceptable emergency equipment includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles, six fuses or three liquid burning flares, and a properly charged fire extinguisher.
